description: FHWA's resilience pilots page maps the pilots it ran with state departments of transportation, metropolitan planning organisations and others to develop and deploy resilience solutions to current and future extreme weather, with links to study reports. It includes nine engineering case studies of the Transportation Engineering Approaches to Resiliency project, such as roadways on permafrost, wildfire and precipitation impacts on a culvert on US 34 in Colorado, a living shoreline for Shore Road in Brookhaven, New York, and slope stability on Interstate 77 in Virginia. An Alaska pilot assessed shoreline erosion at the Kivalina runway and permafrost melt at Igloo Creek and along the Dalton Highway. Coverage: sites across the United States. Format and access: web map and free reports. Licence and cost: free to read; no licence is stated on the page. Caveats: studies differ in method and date. It supports climate adaptation, hazard exposure and resilience studies of road and airport assets. It relates to the Gulf Coast study for Mobile and the FHWA Emergency Relief resilience case studies in the catalogue.
